<H2> Learn and practise <LINE> <TEXT> Close this guide and choose Read on the magazine to learn the style. Opening these pages alone does not teach it. Finish reading; interrupted reading does not grant the style. <LINE> <LINE> Martial Arts is one skill, from level 0 to 10, shared by every style. Each level raises your attack speed and damage and lowers the endurance each strike costs. Every style also has its own hidden mastery, from 0 to 5. Landing hits with a style trains the skill and that style's mastery. You begin with two combinations. Each mastery level unlocks four more, longer ones, and mastery 2, 3, 4 and 5 each unlock a special, which is a heavy attack. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Controls <LINE> <TEXT> Keep both hands free of ordinary equipment. Aim and attack to begin. Hold attack to continue the combination; release it to finish the current strike. Release aim to cancel. Aim toward a fallen zombie and use the floor-attack control when necessary. <LINE> <LINE> Right-click the ground and choose Martial Arts, or press K, to open the Martial Arts window. Choose the style you fight with there and see each style's mastery and everything it unlocks; click an unlocked heavy attack of your active style to equip it. Default keys: Backslash cycles learned styles; R uses the equipped special; K opens the window. All of them can be rebound in Options. <LINE> <LINE> Every strike costs endurance, including misses. Moving strikes cost 12% more, and each skill level improves efficiency and stance footwork. Watch your endurance. Higher skill improves speed but does not remove fatigue or attack recovery. Specials have no timed cooldown.

Slow, ordinary strikes available to everyone. Mastery levels 1-4 add body straight, one-two, short knee and straight-hook. At mastery 5, Grab and Knee unlocks as your only heavy attack. Equip it in the Martial Arts window and use the heavy-attack control (R by default). Eight normal attack choices and one heavy at full mastery, with modest speed and damage gains. At close range, the knee and jab-knee can grab a standing zombie by the head. Use the normal shove control for emergency separation.

<H1> Boxing <LINE> <TEXT> Work behind the jab. Slip and roll under punches, then counter with hooks, uppercuts, body shots and the overhand right. The rear cross and uppercuts deliver your strongest punches. Short combinations conserve endurance; a long flurry leaves less room to disengage. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> A grounded opponent <LINE> <TEXT> Aim at the floor to drop into a crouching hammer punch, then recover before moving on.

<H1> Karate <LINE> <TEXT> Alternate lead and reverse punches with snapping kicks. Front, side and roundhouse kicks lead into spinning hook, spinning back and jumping kicks. Keep enough space to recover from the heavier techniques. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> A grounded opponent <LINE> <TEXT> Aim at the floor for a leaping heel stomp. At Karate mastery 4, hold Shift and press your special key for the running flying kick. You do not need to aim first.

<H1> Mixed martial arts <LINE> <TEXT> Mix punches, elbows, knees and kicks. Enter with straights or a superman punch, work the body, then finish with hooks, a spinning backfist or a flying knee. Leg kicks create a different entry into punching range. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> A grounded opponent <LINE> <TEXT> Aim at the floor for a diving punch. The double-leg takedown is a separate special, unlocked at MMA mastery 5, with a paired ground-and-pound sequence. That finisher supports solo and experimental hosted/dedicated multiplayer testing. A server reservation prevents two players from mounting the same zombie. <LINE> <LINE> To use the finisher, reach MMA mastery 5, right-click the ground > Martial Arts > Equipped special and choose Double-leg takedown and ground-and-pound. Keep both hands free, face a standing zombie within five tiles, aim and press R. Your character walks into position, grabs and completes the sequence. You can release right-click; incidental movement inputs do not cancel it. Press Space to cancel. Start with at least 35% endurance. It begins with a standing takedown; a zombie already on the floor is not an entry target.

<H1> Muay Thai <LINE> <TEXT> Use the push kick to manage distance. Round kicks follow the hands; elbows, spinning and jumping elbows and knees punish opponents at close range. Heavy kicks cost more endurance than setup punches. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> A grounded opponent <LINE> <TEXT> Aim at the floor to leap and drop onto a fallen opponent, then return to your high guard.

Control distance with kicks and light footwork. Mastery unlocks twenty-two combinations, including jumping and tornado-kick chains. Back, hook, turning and axe kicks are heavy attacks. Longer combinations need more room and stamina.
